title: Suspected Cardiac Arrest
attribution: American Heart Association / Red Cross Guidelines
overview: Victim is unresponsive, not breathing normally, or only gasping.
steps: Check scene safety and tap victim's shoulder shouting 'Are you OK?'.
If unresponsive and not breathing, immediately call emergency services or activate SOS.
Place heel of one hand in center of chest, place other hand on top and interlock fingers.
Push hard and fast: 100-120 compressions/min, at least 2 inches (5 cm) deep.
Allow chest to fully recoil between each compression.
Continue uninterrupted CPR until emergency responders arrive or an AED is ready.
warnings: Do NOT stop chest compressions for more than 10 seconds.
Do NOT hesitate to perform hands-only CPR even if untrained in rescue breaths.

title: Severe Bleeding & Hemorrhage
attribution: Stop the Bleed / WHO First Aid Manual
overview: Spurting or continuous rapid blood flow from a traumatic wound.
steps: Ensure personal safety; use disposable gloves or barrier if available.
Expose the wound by cutting or removing clothing.
Apply direct, continuous, firm pressure onto the bleeding point using sterile gauze, towel, or cloth.
Maintain unbroken pressure for at least 5 to 10 minutes without lifting the dressing.
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top; NEVER remove the original layers.
If bleeding is from an arm/leg and life-threatening, apply a certified tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound.
warnings: Do NOT remove embedded objects (knife, glass) — stabilize them in place.
Do NOT release pressure to check if bleeding has stopped.

title: Road Traffic Accident (RTA)
overview: High-velocity vehicular or motorcycle impact involving trauma.
steps: Secure scene: Warn oncoming traffic using hazard lights or indicators. Turn off vehicle ignition.
DO NOT move the casualty unless there is immediate threat of fire, explosion, or submersion.
Stabilize cervical spine: Manually hold the head and neck in neutral alignment without twisting.
If motorcyclist is breathing, DO NOT remove the helmet unless airway is obstructed.
Check airway and breathing without tilting the neck excessively (use jaw-thrust maneuver if trained).
Control any major external bleeding with direct pressure.
Cover victim to maintain body temperature and prevent hypovolemic shock.
warnings: Moving a spinal trauma victim can cause permanent quadriplegia or death.
Do NOT give oral liquids or medication to trauma victims.

title: Choking (Airway Obstruction)
overview: Victim cannot breathe, speak, or cough, and may clutch their throat.
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' If victim nods and cannot cough, intervene immediately.
Stand behind the victim with one foot forward for balance.
Deliver 5 sharp back blows between shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
If obstruction remains: Wrap arms around victim's waist, make a fist above the navel.
Grasp fist with other hand and pull sharply inward and upward (Heimlich maneuver).
Repeat sequence of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object clears or victim becomes unresponsive.
warnings: If victim loses consciousness, lower them gently to ground and start CPR immediately.
Do NOT perform blind finger sweeps in mouth.

title: Burns & Scalds
overview: Thermal, chemical, or contact burns to skin tissue.
steps: Cool the burn immediately under cool, gentle running water for 10 to 20 minutes.
Remove jewelry and loose clothing around the burn before swelling occurs.
Cover burn loosely with a sterile, non-adherent dressing or clean cling wrap.
Keep patient warm with a blanket over unburned areas.
Seek emergency medical evaluation for burns larger than the patient's palm, on face, hands, joints, or groin.
warnings: Do NOT apply ice, butter, toothpaste, or oil to burns.
Do NOT peel off clothing that is stuck to melted or charred skin.

title: Seizures & Convulsions
overview: Involuntary shaking, muscular rigidity, or loss of responsiveness.
steps: Gently guide person to the ground to prevent falling.
Clear away sharp, hard, or hot objects.
Place a soft folded jacket or cushion under the person's head.
Loosen tight neckwear (ties, collars).
Time the seizure. If it lasts longer than 5 minutes, call ambulance immediately.
Once shaking stops, gently roll person onto their side into recovery position to keep airway clear.
warnings: Do NOT hold the person down or restrain their movements.
Do NOT put ANYTHING in the person's mouth.

title: Falls & Suspected Fractures
overview: Severe localized pain, swelling, deformity, or inability to bear weight after a fall.
steps: Encourage casualty to remain still; do not force movement of injured limb.
Support the injured area in the most comfortable position using rolled blankets or splints.
If bone pierces skin (open fracture), cover with clean dressing; apply pressure around edges to stop bleeding.
Apply cold pack wrapped in a cloth to reduce swelling (max 15 mins).
Check circulation below injury (warmth, sensation, pulse).
warnings: Do NOT attempt to push back protruding bone ends or realign crooked limbs.
Do NOT massage the injured limb.

title: Electric Shock
attribution: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Guidance
overview: Contact with energized electrical line or household appliance.
steps: DO NOT TOUCH THE VICTIM while they are still in contact with electrical source.
Turn off the power source or unplug appliance immediately at breaker box.
If unable to cut power, use a dry non-conductive object (wooden broom handle) to push victim clear.
Once safe from current, check responsiveness and breathing; begin CPR if pulseless.
Treat visible entrance/exit burn points with clean dry dressings.
warnings: Never touch high-voltage power lines until certified utility personnel disconnect current.
Do NOT use damp or metal objects to move victim.

title: Unconsciousness (Breathing Normally)
overview: Person is unresponsive but chest rises regularly with clear airway sounds.
steps: Kneel beside person, ensure their legs are straight.
Place the arm nearest to you at a right angle to body, elbow bent with palm up.
Bring far arm across chest, hold back of hand against person's near cheek.
With your other hand, pull the far knee up until foot is flat on ground.
Roll person toward you onto their side by pulling the raised knee.
Tilt head backward gently to maintain open airway, mouth facing downward to allow fluids to drain.
warnings: If spinal injury is suspected, only roll victim if airway is threatened by vomiting.
Monitor breathing continuously until paramedics arrive.
